applyList.issue: The vocab item is the verb 놓다 (to place/put), but the sentence uses the noun 논 (rice field) — the targetForm field is even '논'. The sentence is grammatically fine Korean but does not exemplify 놓다 in any form; 논 is an unrelated homograph of the bare stem.

굴다 takes the [adverb]-게 굴다 pattern (e.g., 무례하게 굴다, 버릇없이 굴다); 굴게 inverts this since 굴다 is not used adverbially. Additionally, 굴다 and 행동하다 are near-synonyms ('to act/behave'), so stacking them is redundant.
Honorific mismatch confirmed: with 할아버지 as subject, standard Korean usage requires honorific verb 주신다 (and ideally honorific particle 께서). 할아버지가 ... 준다 reads as disrespectful in normal usage.
푸다 is the only 우-irregular verb in Korean: the stem 푸 + 어 contracts to 퍼, never 푸어. Correct present polite form is 퍼요, not 푸어요.

applyList.newKorean: 잠자기 전에 불을 끄는 것이 좋아요.
applyList.issue: The -(으)ㅁ nominalization 끔 is heavily formal/written and is rarely used as a clausal subject in conversational sentences. Standard natural Korean uses -는 것 here: 끄는 것이 좋아요 / 끄는 게 좋아요. 끔이 좋아요 sounds stilted and machine-translated.
The vocab item is 나다 (to occur/come out), but the sentence uses 떠나다 (to leave). The targetForm '난다고' is just a substring of 떠난다고. The Korean is fine, but it does not exemplify the lemma 나다.
넣다 + -어 두다 should give 넣어 두었어요. The form 너 is wrong — it looks like a truncation/typo of 넣어. The sentence is currently ungrammatical.
The -(으)ㅁ nominalization 드림 as a clausal subject is awkward and overly formal. Native phrasing uses -는 것: 드리는 것이 예의예요. As written, it reads as machine-translated.

들치다 means to lift/raise the edge or corner of a covering (e.g., 천막을 들치다, 이불을 들치다). For tipping a hat as a greeting Koreans say 모자를 들어 인사하다 (raise the hat) or 모자를 벗어 인사하다 (take it off). 모자를 들치고 인사하다 is an unnatural collocation.

Involuntary trembling from cold/fear takes the intransitive 떨리다 (손이 떨리다, 손이 떨려요). The transitive 손을 떨다 implies a deliberate, voluntary shaking — pairing it with 추워서 (because it's cold) is unnatural; cold doesn't cause one to shake one's hands on purpose.
Honorific mismatch confirmed: 할머니 as subject normally takes the honorific verb (짜신다) and ideally honorific particle 께서. The plain form 짠다 reads as disrespectful in standard usage.
울려 퍼지다 means 'to resonate/echo and spread,' used exclusively for sounds. 웅크리기 (Defense Curl) is a silent self-targeting pose, so it cannot 울려 퍼지다. The collocation is unnatural in Korean.
울려 퍼지다 is a sound-only verb. 알낳기 (Soft-Boiled) is a silent healing move. Saying it 'echoed across the field' is not idiomatic Korean.
울려 퍼지다 requires a sound subject. 각지기 (Sharpen) is a non-acoustic stat-up move; it cannot resonate or echo across a field.
울려 퍼지다 is for sounds. 아침햇살 (Morning Sun) is light/healing — sunlight 비치다/내리쬐다, not 울려 퍼지다. The collocation is wrong.
본러쉬 (Bone Rush) is a physical bone-throwing combo, not a sound. Pairing it with 울려 퍼지다 ('to resonate and spread') is awkward; a physical attack does not echo across a field in Korean.
Smog/gas spreads or drifts (퍼지다 is fine alone, but 울려 퍼지다 specifically means sound resonating). Gas does not 울리다, so this is the wrong verb pairing.
천사의키스 (Sweet Kiss) is a status move, not a sound. The 울려 퍼지다 collocation requires an audible subject; this pairing is unidiomatic.
연속자르기 (Fury Cutter) is a series of physical slashes, not a sound. 울려 퍼지다 is reserved for sound; the collocation is off.
환상빔 (Psybeam) is a beam of energy, not a sound. 울려 퍼지다 needs an audible subject. A 빔 normally 발사되다 / 뻗어 나가다, not 울려 퍼지다.
메가드레인 (Mega Drain) is an HP-absorbing move, silent and non-acoustic. The 울려 퍼지다 collocation is incorrect; nothing audible is being produced.
악몽 (Nightmare) is a mental status condition, not a sound. 울려 퍼지다 requires an audible subject. Even metaphorically, nightmares 'spread' (퍼지다) but do not 울리다.
버섯포자 (Spore) is airborne particles. Spores 날리다/퍼지다 but never 울리다. 울려 퍼지다 is the wrong verb for a non-sound subject.

Confirmed: attaching the topic particle 는 directly to the dictionary form 깨트리다 produces a parse collision with the quotative reduction -ㄴ다는 / -다는. Korean readers will hear 깨트리다는 as a malformed quotative rather than 'the move 깨트리다'. The fix uses the (이)라는 naming particle which is the standard way to cite a name/term in Korean.

Same parse collision as 깨트리다는: 뛰어오르다 is a verb in dictionary form, and attaching 는 produces what reads as a malformed quotative -다는 rather than topic-marking a noun. Use the (이)라는 naming particle to cite the move name as a name.

Confirmed broken: 탐내다가 parses as the connective -다가 ('while coveting...'), giving 'while coveting, it echoed across the field' — nonsensical. The fix cites the move name with the 라는 naming particle and uses 기술이 as the actual subject of 울려 퍼지다.

applyList.originalKorean: 클리어바디 특성가 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.newKorean: 클리어바디 특성이 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.issue: Wrong subject particle. 특성 ends in the consonant ㅇ (받침), so it must take 이, not 가. '특성가' is ungrammatical.

applyList.originalKorean: 천하장사 특성가 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.newKorean: 천하장사 특성이 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.issue: Wrong subject particle. 특성 ends in a consonant (받침 ㅇ) and must take 이. '특성가' is ungrammatical.

applyList.originalKorean: 탈피 특성가 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.newKorean: 탈피 특성이 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.issue: Wrong subject particle. 특성 ends in a consonant (받침 ㅇ) and must take 이. '특성가' is ungrammatical.

applyList.originalKorean: 돌머리 특성가 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.newKorean: 돌머리 특성이 시합에서 큰 도움이 됐어요.
applyList.issue: Wrong subject particle. 특성 ends in a consonant (받침 ㅇ) and must take 이. '특성가' is ungrammatical.

Confirmed particle error: for storage/accumulation in a place, the locative 에 is required. 볼에서 marks the cheeks as the SOURCE from which electricity is gathered, contradicting the Pokemon-canonical description that Pikachu STORES electricity in pouches inside its cheeks (official Korean pokedex: '볼 안쪽의 작은 전기 주머니'). 볼에 전기를 모아요 = stores electricity in its cheeks.

전기를 흘리다 is not a natural Korean collocation. 흘리다 is normally used with liquids/tears/blood, with 'information' (정보를 흘리다 = to leak), or with sweat. For releasing/discharging electricity, native usage employs 방출하다, 발산하다, or 흘려보내다. As-is the sentence reads roughly like 'Raichu drips/leaks very strong electricity', which is unidiomatic.

applyList.newKorean: 콘팡은 큰 눈으로 어둠 속에서도 잘 봐요.
applyList.issue: 어둠을 보다 literally means 'to see darkness' and is only used in metaphorical/literary senses (e.g. seeing the darkness within oneself). The intended meaning per the gloss is 'sees in the dark' / 'sees through the darkness', which in natural Korean is 어둠 속에서도 잘 봐요 or 어두운 곳에서도 잘 봐요. As written, the sentence does not convey night vision and sounds odd.

The gloss says 'uses powerful psychic abilities', but 정신력 means 'willpower / mental fortitude', not psychic ability. Golduck's psychic powers in Korean Pokédex/wiki are described with 초능력 or 염력 (telekinesis). As written, the sentence says Golduck uses strong willpower, mismatching the gloss. (Same kind of mistranslation appears for 뮤츠 in the rest of the file.)

불꽃이 타다 ('flames burn') is semantically redundant — 불꽃 already implies burning. Natural Korean uses 불꽃이 일다, 불꽃이 타오르다, or 불꽃이 피어오르다 for flames rising/blazing from a place. As is, the sentence sounds tautological and slightly off.

applyList.newKorean: 또도가스는 머리가 두 개인 모습으로 진화했어요.
applyList.issue: 머리가 두 개로 진화했어요 literally says 'evolved AS [its] heads becoming two', which is structurally awkward — the subject of 진화하다 is the Pokémon, not the heads. Native phrasing would express the result either as '머리가 두 개로 늘었어요' (heads increased to two) or '머리가 두 개인 모습으로 진화했어요' (evolved into a form with two heads).

'분노를 가지다' (to have/possess anger) is grammatically possible but not a natural Korean collocation. Native speakers would normally say '분노에 차 있다', '몹시 분노한다', or use an adjective like '사납다'. The verb 가지다 is typically used with possessable nouns or stable traits, not transient strong emotions like 분노.

applyList.newKorean: 샤미드는 이브이가 물 타입으로 진화한 모습이에요.
applyList.issue: '물 타입으로 진화한 이브이예요' literally says 'It is an Eevee that has evolved into Water type', which is awkward because once Eevee evolves it is no longer an Eevee. More natural Korean phrasing would treat Vaporeon as the result/form of Eevee's evolution rather than describing it as an Eevee.

The gloss says 'powerful psychic abilities', but 정신력 means 'willpower / mental fortitude / resolve', not psychic powers. The correct Korean for 'psychic abilities' is 초능력 (or 사이코파워 in some Pokémon contexts). As written, the Korean describes Mewtwo as having strong willpower, which mistranslates the original.

applyList.newKorean: 에브이는 이브이가 마음의 힘으로 진화한 모습이에요.
applyList.issue: Same structural issue as the 샤미드 entry: '진화한 이브이예요' is awkward because Espeon, having evolved, is no longer an Eevee. Korean speakers typically describe an Eeveelution as the evolved 모습/포켓몬 of Eevee, not as an Eevee itself.
Same particle error as 피카츄. The intended meaning is 'gathers/accumulates electricity in both arms' (location of storage), which requires the locative 에. 두 팔에서 reads as 'from both arms' (source).

applyList.newKorean: 칠색조는 일곱 가지 색의 깃털을 가졌어요.
applyList.issue: The gloss says 'Ho-Oh has feathers of seven colors', but the Korean translates literally to 'Ho-Oh has seven kinds of light/color' with no mention of 깃털 (feathers). 빛 can poetically mean color, but the gloss's specific reference to feathers is dropped, producing a notable mismatch between the Korean and the English gloss.

applyList.newKorean: 포켓몬 센터에서 치료를 받았어요. (or: 포켓몬 센터에서 포켓몬을 회복시켰어요.)
applyList.issue: '회복을 받다' (literally 'to receive recovery') is not a natural Korean collocation. 회복 is something one does or undergoes, not receives. For Pokemon Center healing, native usage would be '치료를 받았어요' (received treatment) or '포켓몬을 회복시켰어요' (had my Pokemon recovered). The targetForm vocab '회복' could still be exercised via 회복하다/회복시키다.

applyList.originalKorean: 가방 안에 회복약이 다섯 개 있어요.
applyList.newKorean: 가방 안에 상처약이 다섯 개 있어요.
applyList.issue: 회복약 is real Korean but the canonical Pokemon-game term for Potion in Korean releases is 상처약 (confirmed on Pokemon Wiki KO and 나무위키 회복 도구 page). For a Pokemon-themed deck, the in-game term is more authentic and reinforces vocabulary the player will see in the game.

Confirmed Pokemon-lore mismatch: Ivysaur's defining feature is the flower BUD (꽃봉오리) on its back, not a 새싹 (sprout/seedling). The bud is a Rafflesia-like flower bud that releases an aroma when ready to bloom. 새싹 is more apt for Bulbasaur (이상해씨); by Ivysaur stage the plant has progressed to a large bud.

applyList.originalKorean: 이상해꽃은 큰 꽃을 등에 가지고 있어요.
applyList.newKorean: 이상해꽃은 등에 큰 꽃이 피어 있어요.
applyList.issue: '꽃을 등에 가지고 있다' (literally 'has a flower on its back') is grammatically valid but unidiomatic in Korean for describing a body feature. Native phrasings would be '등에 큰 꽃이 피어 있어요' (a flower is blooming on its back) or '등에 큰 꽃을 달고 있어요' (carries a flower on its back). The current phrasing reads like a literal English-to-Korean translation.

'불꽃이 타다' is grammatically valid (타다 covers 'for fire/flame to burn') but is awkward as a stand-alone description; Korean more typically uses 불꽃이 타오르다 (flame blazes), 불꽃이 일다 (flame arises), or 불이 타다. For Charmander's tail flame the canonical Korean phrasing is '꼬리에 불이 타고 있다' or '꼬리 끝에서 불꽃이 타올라요'.

applyList.originalKorean: 갑은 거북 등껍질을 뜻하는 옛 글자예요.
applyList.issue: Confirmed terminology error: 갑(甲) is a Sino-Korean 한자 (Chinese character), specifically a 상형문자 (pictograph) modeled on the shape of a turtle's shell. '옛 글자' is misleading because in Korean it commonly evokes 옛한글 (archaic hangul). Naver/나무위키 갑골문자 entries describe 甲 as a 한자 / 상형문자. Adding the 한자 in parentheses also helps disambiguate the homophone.

applyList.newKorean: 강철은 '강한 쇠'라는 뜻으로, 단단하게 만든 철을 가리켜요.
applyList.issue: Gloss says '강철 means hardened steel' (a metalinguistic etymology gloss), but the Korean literally says '강철 is a hard metal'. The Korean omits the etymology framing entirely and just states a fact. For an etymology-roots entry the Korean should reflect the meaning of 강철 as a root ('강' = strong/hard + '철' = iron → steel) rather than a definition of 'steel'. Also 강철 specifically means 'steel', not 'hard metal' generically.

몰다 means to drive (a car, a herd of animals), not to ride a bicycle. The standard Korean collocation for bicycles is 자전거를 타다. 자전거를 몰다 is unnatural and would strike native speakers as wrong; 몰다 only fits motorized vehicles like 차/오토바이 or animals being driven (소떼를 몰다).

applyList.newKorean: 이 잡지는 제5호예요. (or, for a book: 이 책은 제5권이에요.)
applyList.issue: 호 is the counter for issues of periodicals (magazines, journals, newsletters), not for 책 in the general 'book' sense. Calling a 책 'the 5호' implies it is issue #5 of a serial — odd for a generic book. Standard counter for books is 권. Also 제5호 is conventionally written without an internal space.

Word order is reversed. The natural Korean for 'powdered/icing sugar' is 가루 설탕 (modifier-head: powder-form sugar) or 슈가 파우더. 설탕 가루 (sugar's powder) reads as a redundant tautology since 설탕 itself already denotes a granular substance. Native bakers say 가루 설탕을 뿌려요.

applyList.newKorean: 책을 두 권 빌렸어요. (or, if the same-copy sense is intended: 그 책을 두 부 빌렸어요.)
applyList.issue: Two issues. (1) 부 is the counter for printed copies of newspapers/documents/the same-edition reprint of a book; the unmarked counter for books is 권 (책 두 권). (2) The numeral-counter-의-noun structure (두 부의 책) is stilted; native pattern places the counter phrase post-nominally: 책 두 부를 빌렸어요. Combined, the sentence sounds translation-flavored.

While 멋이 있다 is grammatically possible, native speakers overwhelmingly use the contracted adjective 멋있다 to mean 'is stylish/cool'. The decomposed form 멋이 있다 with a topic-marked location (옷에는) reads as a stilted calque ('there is style in his clothes'). Standard: 그의 옷이 멋있어요.

The standard term for the body of traffic rules drivers/pedestrians follow is 교통 법규 or 교통 규칙 (or the formal statute name 도로교통법, no internal space). 교통 법 (with a space, just '법') is unidiomatic — 법 alone is the abstract noun 'law' and pairs with major bodies of law (헌법, 형법) rather than with everyday compliance. Native speakers say 교통 법규를 지키다 / 교통 규칙을 지키다.

묻다 'to ask' is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel, so the past tense is 물었어요, not 묻었어요. The form 묻었어요 is the regular conjugation of the homonym 묻다 'to bury' — semantically wrong here. Standard form: 선생님께 길을 물었어요.
Sino-Korean numeral 육 should not be used with the native counter 개. Counting discrete physical objects (apples) requires native numerals: 사과 여섯 개. Mixing 육 + 개 sounds wrong to native speakers.
Korean orthography rule (한글 맞춤법): administrative-unit suffixes such as 구/시/도/군/동 attach to the place name with no space. Should be 강남구, written as one word.
When 분 means 'minutes', it requires Sino-Korean numerals (오 분), not native (다섯). 다섯 분 reads as 'five people (honorific)' — exactly the wrong sense for the gloss 'five minutes'.

오르다 collocates with 산에/산을, not 산 위에. 산 위에 올라가다/오르다 is a known learner-style overspecification — 위에 redundantly stacks the upward sense already inherent in 오르다, and 위에 normally pairs with stative 있다, not motion 오르다.

applyList.originalKorean: 이 길과 저 길 중 선택을 해요.
applyList.newKorean: 이 길과 저 길 중에서 선택하세요.
applyList.issue: The Korean is plain declarative (-아요/-어요), meaning 'I/we choose...', but the English gloss is the imperative 'Choose between this road and that road.' For an imperative the Korean should be 선택하세요 / 선택해요(명령) with appropriate intonation, or be reglossed as a statement.

The fixed expression is 한잔하다 / 소주(를) 한잔하다 — typically written without 를 between 소주 and 한잔, or as 소주 한 잔 했어요 with no object marker. Adding 를 to 소주 here makes 한 잔 하다 read as a literal 'did one glass', breaking the idiom. The natural form is 어른들이 소주를 한잔했어요 or 어른들이 소주 한 잔 하셨어요.

Grammatical but pragmatically odd. 밥을 짓다 is correct Korean (HiNative confirms it as the standard, slightly literary expression for cooking rice). However, a 농부 (farmer) prototypically '농사를 짓다' (does farming), not '밥을 짓다' in their professional capacity. Native speakers would naturally pair 밥을 짓다 with 어머니/할머니. Switching to 어머니 keeps the headword 짓다 with its most idiomatic collocation and removes the cognitive friction.
Spacing error. The suffix 식 (style) attaches directly to the preceding noun, so it should be written 한국식 as one word (or use 한식). 한국 식 with a space is non-standard.
Awkward collocation. 가로 means horizontal width, and width is normally described with 좁다 (narrow) rather than 짧다 (short). 가로가 짧다 sounds odd to native ears; 가로 길이가 짧다 or 가로가 좁다 would be more natural.
Spacing error. The bound noun 거 attaches to the demonstrative without a space: standard form is 그거 (or 그것). 그 거 with a space is non-standard orthography.
쓰레기통 (trash bin) is a single dictionary word; the sentence splits it as 쓰레기를 ... 통에, where 통에 alone could mean any container. Natural Korean would be 쓰레기통에 버리세요.
Spacing error. 북쪽 is one word in the standard Korean dictionary and must not be split with a space.
Spacing error. 여 is a bound prefix; 여학생 (female student) is a single dictionary word. 여 학생 with a space is incorrect — 여 cannot stand alone.

이렇다 is overwhelmingly used either attributively (이런 + noun) or in its 반말/요체 contracted forms (이래/이래요). Standalone 날씨가 이렇네요 is grammatical only as a deictic comment requiring a shared visible referent (gesturing at bad weather), which a flashcard cannot supply. As a textbook sentence it reads as incomplete. Reframing with 이렇다 inside a 이런 ~ 날씨 attributive structure makes the headword's usage pattern clearer and is unambiguously well-formed in isolation.
피시 in Korean is overwhelmingly read as PC (personal computer) and is not the standard word for fish. Catching fish uses 물고기 or 생선. 피시를 잡다 is unnatural and confusing — it reads as 'catches PCs well'.
Spacing error. 고속도로 (highway) is a single dictionary entry and should be written as one word. 고속 도로 with a space is non-standard.

Spacing error. 벚 is a bound morpheme that cannot stand alone; 벚꽃 is the established word for cherry blossom. The sentence should be either 벚꽃잎이... or 벚꽃 잎이... — 벚 꽃잎 splits the wrong morpheme boundary.

Confirmed pedagogical issue: the headword 동물 appears only as a substring of 동물원 (zoo); the standalone word 동물 is never exemplified. For a vocabulary card teaching 동물, the example must contain 동물 as an independent token. The proposed fix keeps the zoo theme but introduces 동물 itself.

applyList.originalKorean: 퇴근 후에 맥주를 한 잔 해요.
applyList.newKorean: 퇴근 후에 맥주 한 잔 해요.
applyList.issue: The collocation '맥주를 한 잔 하다' with the object particle 를 sounds awkward. Native speakers either drop the particle ('맥주 한 잔 해요') or use the verb 마시다 ('맥주를 한 잔 마셔요'). The pattern 'X 한 잔 하다' typically appears without 를.
'초의 불꽃' is overly literal/stilted. Natives use the compound 촛불 ('candle flame/light'). '초의 불꽃' reads as a translation from English 'the candle's flame'.

applyList.newKorean: 그 사람은 친절하다고 알려져 있어요. (or: 그 사람은 친절한 사람으로 불려요.)
applyList.issue: 불리다 ('to be called/named') normally takes a noun complement via -(이)라고 불리다 ('is called X-name'), e.g. '천재라고 불려요'. Pairing it with the descriptive clause 친절하다고 ('that he is kind') is unnatural; for being known/described as having a quality, 알려져 있다 or 평가받다 is the right verb.

applyList.newKorean: 이 기계는 사용하기 어렵네요. (or: 이 기계의 사용법이 어렵네요.)
applyList.issue: '사용이 어렵다' as a predicate sounds like translationese. Natural Korean prefers a verbal nominalization: '사용하기 어렵다' or the compound '사용법이 어렵다'.

수 in the sense of 'a number' is rarely used as a stand-alone count noun in colloquial Korean; native speakers say 숫자 ('이 숫자가 정확해요'). 수 alone reads as bookish/abstract and is hard to parse without context.

Confirmed parse ambiguity: 길이 can be tokenized either as 길+이 (subject-marked 'road') or as 길이 (the noun 'length'). Native readers may briefly garden-path. Korean parsing literature (Eojoel ambiguity) documents this exact class of segmentation problem. Dropping the redundant subject particle (양쪽 길 모두 ...) eliminates the ambiguity and matches the more natural collocation.
봐 보세요 stacks 보다 + -아 보다 ('try seeing') with itself, producing an awkward double imperative. The standard form is simply 자세히 보세요 or 자세히 살펴보세요.

With the topic-marked subject 이 의자는 and no agent, the active 만들었어요 reads as 'this chair made [something] out of iron'. To say 'this chair is made of iron' Korean requires the passive 만들어졌어요 (or the relative clause 만든).
